summary.headline: SMC Global Q1 FY27 consolidated operating income rose 21.2% YoY to ₹515.1 crore and PAT rose 22.3% to ₹36.7 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated operating income reached ₹515.1 crore (+21.2% YoY) with EBITDA of ₹107 crore (+6.9% YoY, 20.9% margin) and PAT of ₹36.7 crore versus ₹30 crore in Q1 FY26. Broking, distribution and trading drove growth, with cash-market mix rising and derivatives softer. Insurance broking revenue grew 44.4% but segment EBIT was only ₹1.6 crore due to investment in manpower. The NBFC segment's AUM fell QoQ to ₹1,025 crore, and management is now targeting a lower year-end AUM than earlier guidance implied.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹30 crore in Q1 FY26, +22.3% YoY

segments.name: Broking, distribution & trading
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹316.3 crore (+15.1% YoY) and EBIT ₹74.3 crore (+17.6% YoY); 13.8 lakh client accounts including StoxKart and 92,129 active SIPs. Cash-market brokerage share reportedly rose from 45% to 55%.

segments.name: Insurance broking
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹167.3 crore (+44.4% YoY) with EBIT of ₹1.6 crore; gross premium ₹759 crore, 2.7 lakh policies, 16,747 POS agents. Non-life is about 90% of premium; EBIT moderated on manpower investment.

segments.name: Financing (NBFC, Moneywise)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹46.5 crore and EBIT ₹26.1 crore; AUM ₹1,025 crore across 40 branches in 7 states. Secured book is 75% of AUM; LAP (about ₹50 crore) and unsecured business loans (about ₹40 crore) declined in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: NBFC AUM expected to close FY27 at ₹1,250-1,300 crore, versus the earlier guidance of about 25% growth that management acknowledged was missed.
NBFC AUM longer-term aim is 20-25% CAGR, but management said investors should wait a year or two because of run-off from discontinued products.
Cost of funds fell about 25 bps in the quarter; management expects NIM to rise gradually over coming years on higher-yield retail mix.
Management expects Q2 to be 'much better' and the coming year to be much better than last year, citing market activity.
Long-term target of about 20% revenue CAGR; management cited a five-year revenue range of ₹6,000-8,000 crore and PAT rising from ₹103 crore to about ₹170 crore, but declined to give formal figures.
StoxKart revenue has increased about four times YoY, and management is positive on its subscription model.
capex_capacity: Investment in technology and AI: in-app AI chatbot on a proprietary language model, AI-based algo platform launched; AI insights feature in mobile app in testing with launch expected soon.
Insurance broking spending on manpower in corporate and life insurance, plus distribution capacity and technology ahead of a reinsurance opportunity after composite broker upgrade.
Distribution network: 16,747 POS/cost network, 385 Motor Insurance Service Providers, 40 NBFC branches across 7 states.
demand_pricing: Management attributed broking growth to Nifty and Sensex gains of about 6-7%, DII buying above ₹2 lakh crore against FPI selling of about ₹1.5 lakh crore, and a shift from derivatives to cash market.
MTF and T+5 book rose from ₹760 crore to over ₹900 crore.
StoxKart added about 26,000 subscription clients in the quarter; its revenue was about ₹20 crore in Q1 FY27, per management.
Mutual fund AUM growth came partly from market appreciation and partly from net mobilisation through training, investor awareness and the Easy Invest digital platform.
NBFC: secured retail products (micro LAP, gold loan) are growing; yields are rising as the mix shifts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NBFC AUM miss the earlier ~25% growth guidance, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Gupta said AUM was ₹1,025 crore versus ₹1,118 crore in March 2026. LAP (about ₹50 crore) and unsecured business loans (about ₹40 crore) declined, and management still expects ₹1,250-1,300 crore by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What drove broking revenue growth despite a weaker derivatives environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Garg cited index gains of about 6-7%, DII inflows, lower crude and easing geopolitics, which shifted activity to cash and delivery. He said the cash brokerage share rose from 45% to 55%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove mutual fund AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Anurag Bansal said MF AUM rose from ₹4,294 crore to ₹4,787 crore (about 11.5%), helped by training, investor awareness and Easy Invest, with part of the gain from market appreciation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did insurance EBIT moderate while revenue grew?
qa_highlights.answer: Sakshi Mehta said spending was mainly on corporate and life insurance manpower, and operating leverage is expected in future quarters. Non-life is about 90% of premium.

qa_highlights.question: How will NBFC funding cost and NIM trend in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Gupta said weighted cost of funds fell about 25 bps, and NIM is expected to grow gradually as the yield mix improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the five-year outlook and quantitative target?
qa_highlights.answer: Subhash Chand Aggarwal cited 20% CAGR and a ₹6,000-8,000 crore revenue range in five years, and PAT of ₹170 crore versus ₹103 crore last year, but declined to give formal figures.
